key_insight: Leading LLMs can generate diverse colonoscopy-prep dialogues, but response correctness varies and unsafe errors remain a concern.
clinical_relevance: Conversational AI could help patients understand prep instructions and ask specific questions, but it should be paired with safety checks and clinician oversight.
method: Generated 250 patient–AI coach dialogues per model across 5 LLMs
Used 3–7 question-answer pairs on diet, medications, and prep topics
Compared human expert ratings with LLM-as-a-judge evaluation and diversity metrics
evidence_signal: The study combined human expert review, automatic evaluation, and permutation tests at the dialogue level to compare correctness, harmfulness, and diversity across models.
watch_item: Synthetic dialogue performance may not translate directly to real patient interactions, so incorrect advice should be filtered and escalated to healthcare providers.
paper_title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Correctness and Diversity in Synthetic Dialogues
